current.title: Why Are 44% Of Rural Homes Still Cooking Over Fire?
current.hook: Rural areas got electricity. Cooking never caught up.
current.closing: Wired up isn't the same as cooked up.
current.question: Does your kitchen run on gas, electric, or fire? Comment below.

segments.say: Rural electricity access jumped from 67 percent in 2000 to 85 percent by 2024 — most of the world's countryside finally got wired up.

segments.topic: why rural cooking never caught up
segments.say: But clean cooking fuel access crawled from just 24 percent to 56 percent — so 44 percent of rural homes are still cooking over open fire or charcoal.

segments.topic: power use behind the rural electricity gap
segments.say: Meanwhile overall electricity use per person climbed from 2,093 to 3,558 kilowatt-hours a year — the world is using more power, just not always the cleanest kind.

problems: The hook (0-4s) has no motion with a purpose: faint unlabeled numbers on an empty gradient.
Irrelevant watermarked stock thumbnails (a winding road, a man walking at sunset) appear in the hook/seg0.
Captions fade to near-invisible grey (seg0:start 'countryside got', seg1:start 'percent in 2000').
Data is decorative: arms raised, riding markers, standing beside a wall that builds itself.
seg3:end: the mascot covers the 55.8 end label.
The headline '44% cooking over fire' is never visualized. The closing gauge shows 55.8, the clean share, not the 44% on fire.
fixes: Replace the hook with a full-frame contrast: a lit bulb over a smoking cookfire, with electricity 85% set against cooking 56%.
Delete the stock thumbnails and the floating number list.
Make the payoff show 44 of 100 homes still with smoke/fire rising, not a clean-fuel dial.
Give Data a real bit: fanning smoke away from a pot, or flipping the light switch and then coughing at the fire.
Keep the mascot clear of value labels, and keep caption opacity at full.
Retitle seg2 honestly as world electricity use per person.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'.
